3	## Document Overview: Core Case + Supporting Retellings
4	
5	The milk-testing dispute case (1889–1925) from Segment 1 continues to be the core narrative across three retellings in Segment 2:
6	- Ivy Keddie's 1959 historical society talk (scientific forensics proving innocence)

8

10	
11	## Cast of Characters and Relationships
12	*(Carried from Segment 1 with additions)*
13	
14	**Ansel Keddie** (Tester, Ostrey Hollow station, 1896–1924)
15	- Ran the skimming station 7 miles up valley from Larrow Green
16	- Kept meticulous test books in his own hand, handwriting "like print," no blots across 29 seasons
17	- Married to Orra Keddie
18	- Denies taking cream: "I have never taken a pound of cream out of that station and there is not a man in this room who thinks I have when he is by himself" (March 1925 statement)
19	- Put out (fired) April 30, 1925, after arbitration award
20	- Died in the 1930s, still under stigma from the 1919 letter
21	- His question mark in the test book about the 1911 anomaly stood unanswered for 14 years
22	- EXONERATED in 1958 (35 years after dismissal, 24 years after death) by scientific analysis
23	
24	**Ivy Keddie** (Granddaughter, historian)
25	- Ansel's granddaughter; Duncan Keddie was her father (teacher at Ashlin)
26	- In 1959, presented findings to Ordell County Historical Society at Ashlin
27	- Conducted scientific forensic analysis of condemned pipettes from 1923
28	- Used calibrated burette to measure nine unbroken pipettes from station crate
29	- Measured pipettes delivering 16.72 cc instead of 17.6 cc (95% of correct volume)
30	- Published findings in Bulletin No. 471 with Professor Vaught
31	
32	**Wilbur Teague** (Bookkeeper, 1905–1945)
33	- Kept the Association's books from 1905 to 1945 (40 years)
34	- Invented the "station-gain" account in 1905 to track difference between credited vs. received butterfat
35	- Station-gain line ran at 5.25 percent of actual cream, year after year
36	- Noted in books: "Ostrey Hollow: butter fat credited to patrons on station test, 57,760 lb. Butter fat received at Larrow Green in station cream, 60,800 lb. Station gain, 3,040 lb, five and a quarter per cent, as usual. Carried to the general account."
37	- Warned Selby Vose about the account in 1916; was told to "let it alone"
38	- Testified at 1925 board of arbitration hearing
39	- Wrote memoir "The Books of the Association" in 1948, three years after retiring
40	- Emphasized: "One man weighed the milk, one man drew the sample, one man made the test, one man wrote the figure... one man ran the separator... no second man in that building from the spring to the fall"
41	- Noted Selby Vose signed the annual sheets every year without comment
42	
43	**Orra Keddie** (Ansel's wife)
44	- First cousin of old Mrs. Vose
45	- Sister of Emmet Brant (largest milk patron)
46	- After 1919 letter, rift with her brother Emmet: "they did not speak. Not one word"
47	- Would walk to Larrow Green rather than pass her brother's lane
48	- Outlived Ansel and suffered the stigma for years after his death
49	
50	**Emmet Brant** (Farmer, Hessel Bottom)
51	- Largest milk patron to Ostrey Hollow station
52	- Brother of Orra Keddie; brother-in-law of Ansel
53	- Stopped speaking to Ansel Keddie after 1919
54	
55	**Gideon Vose** (Association founder and president)
56	- Started the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association in 1889
57	- First president, held office 22 years until 1911
58	- Died in 1917
59	
60	**Selby Vose** (Association manager, 1913–1938)
61	- Son of Gideon Vose
62	- Became manager in 1913
63	- Signed the 1919 circular letter
64	- Signed all annual sheets; Teague brought them to him each spring
65

14	The set of descents is written $D(L)$, and a descent is *cyclic* if the strand containing $i$
15	also contains $i + n \pmod{2n}$.
